name: Content Machine
oneLiner: One brief in, a month of platform-native content out — drafted, checked against your brand rules, and queued for a single approval.
problem: Content dies on consistency, not creativity. A founder posts for three weeks, gets busy, and the channel goes quiet. Hiring it out usually just moves the bottleneck from your calendar to someone else's writing queue.
solution: Content Machine runs the loop: research the angle, draft for each platform, score the draft against your brand rules and a banned-phrase list, rewrite whatever fails, and only then put it in front of you. You approve taste. The machine does the typing.

features.title: Platform-native, not reposted
features.text: One idea becomes an X post, a LinkedIn piece, a caption and a newsletter — each written to its own format, not the same paragraph pasted four times.

features.title: Brand rules as a gate
features.text: Your tone, banned phrases and claims policy are a checklist the draft has to pass. Copy that fails gets rewritten before it ever reaches you.

features.title: Research before drafting
features.text: Every cycle pulls current context on the topic first, so posts reference what is actually happening rather than what a model remembers.

features.title: One approval, not twenty
features.text: The only human step is yes or no. Nothing publishes without you, and nothing reaches you until it has already cleared the gate.

loop.goal: A week of platform-native posts that pass brand, claims and format checks.
loop.verify: Brand-rule, banned-phrase and format lint on every draft, plus a second agent scoring tone against your writing samples.
loop.stop: Every post clears the gate, or six rewrite passes — then it stops and reports what it could not fix.

name: Reputation Machine
oneLiner: Turns quiet happy clients into public reviews, and never leaves a review unanswered.
problem: Clinics, law firms and restaurants live or die on reviews, and the clients who love you are the least likely to say so in public. Meanwhile a one-star review sits unanswered for eleven days because nobody owns the inbox.
solution: Reputation Machine watches your review surfaces, drafts a reply in your voice within minutes of anything landing, and asks for a review at the moment a client is happiest. Anything negative escalates to a person. Nothing angry gets an automated answer.

features.title: Reply drafted before you notice
features.text: A review lands, a reply is drafted in your voice and waiting in your queue. The eleven-day silence stops being a thing that happens.

features.title: Ask at the right moment
features.text: Review requests fire off the events that mean someone is happy — a completed treatment, a closed matter — instead of a monthly blast to your entire list.

features.title: Negative reviews stop at a human
features.text: Anything under your rating threshold is escalated, never auto-published. The machine drafts, a person decides. That line is not configurable.

features.title: Listings that stay consistent
features.text: Hours, address and service data are checked across your listings against one source of truth, so the profile that ranks is the profile that is correct.

loop.goal: Every review answered within the hour, and review volume climbing month over month.
loop.verify: Each reply passes a tone-and-policy check; anything below your rating threshold is blocked from auto-publish; listing data is diffed against your source of truth.
loop.stop: The queue is clear, or a review needs judgment — then it escalates to a human instead of guessing.

name: Answer Engine Machine
oneLiner: Gets your brand cited inside AI answers, then measures honestly whether it worked.
problem: Your customers now ask an assistant instead of clicking a blue link. If the model does not know your brand exists, you are invisible exactly where the decision gets made — and a falling traffic chart will never tell you that is the reason.
solution: Answer Engine Machine builds the structured, entity-rich ground truth an assistant needs in order to quote you, then re-asks the real assistants on a schedule to see whether you actually got cited. It reports coverage and citation frequency. It does not sell you a rank, because AI answers do not have one.

features.title: Entity and schema coverage
features.text: Fills the structured gaps — schema, entities, verifiable facts — that decide whether a model can quote you with confidence or skips you for a competitor.

features.title: Citation-shaped content
features.text: Written the way assistants prefer to quote: direct claims, clean definitions and sourced specifics, instead of a warm introductory paragraph.

features.title: Measured against real assistants
features.text: Runs your priority questions through the actual assistants on a schedule and records whether you were cited — not whether a tool thinks you deserve to be.

features.title: Reporting that stays honest
features.text: Coverage and citation frequency tracked over time. Nobody can promise you rank one in an AI answer, and we will not pretend the number exists.

loop.goal: Named as a source for your priority questions across the major assistants.
loop.verify: Scheduled re-queries against live assistants — a citation either appears in the answer or it does not. There is nothing to argue with.
loop.stop: Coverage target reached, or the run budget is spent — then it reports the remaining gap rather than quietly spending more.

name: Lead Machine
oneLiner: Finds the accounts that look like your best clients, disqualifies the rest, and books the call.
problem: Most outbound fails on relevance, not volume. Buying a bigger list and sending more mail is how a sending domain gets burned and a young brand earns a reputation it cannot undo.
solution: Lead Machine works one narrow, named market: build the list, enrich it, disqualify anything off-profile before a word is written, personalize from real evidence, then send from a warmed domain under hard volume caps. Fewer sends, a higher hit rate, and a domain that survives the quarter.

features.title: Disqualify before you write
features.text: Every account is scored against your profile first. Bad fits are dropped rather than emailed, which is the cheapest way there is to protect a domain.

features.title: Personalized from evidence
features.text: Openers cite something real and checkable about the account, not a spun template wrapped around a merge field that everyone recognizes.

features.title: Deliverability as a hard limit
features.text: Warm-up, volume caps, bounce thresholds, suppression lists and honored opt-outs are enforced by the system — it stops sending before you find out the hard way.

features.title: Booked calls, not open rates
features.text: The only number that counts is meetings on the calendar. Everything above it in the funnel is diagnostics, not a result.

loop.goal: Qualified meetings booked out of one named target market.
loop.verify: Profile-fit score, bounce rate, spam-complaint rate and reply classification — sending halts automatically the moment any threshold trips.
loop.stop: The meeting target is met, or a deliverability threshold trips — then it stops sending and reports rather than pushing through.

name: Hiring Machine
oneLiner: Turns an open role into a vetted Philippine shortlist — sourced, work-sampled, and scored on the same rubric.
problem: US founders know Philippine talent is the best value on the market and still hire badly, because screening a hundred applicants by hand is nobody's full-time job. So the role stays open for a quarter, or the wrong person gets it.
solution: Hiring Machine drafts the role, sources candidates, runs a structured work sample, and scores everyone against one published rubric. It never rejects anyone on its own. What it hands you is a defensible shortlist and the evidence behind each rank.

features.title: Structured, not vibes
features.text: Every candidate answers the same work sample and is scored on the same rubric, so a shortlist is comparable instead of a memory of who interviewed well.

features.title: Evidence over résumé
features.text: Scores come from what a candidate actually produced under the work sample, not from where they went to school or how the CV was formatted.

features.title: A human makes every reject
features.text: The machine ranks and explains its reasoning. It never sends a rejection or filters a person out by itself — that decision carries legal and human weight.

features.title: Built on the SF–Makati seam
features.text: Designed around how US startups actually hire Philippine talent, because it is the way New Machine itself is built.

loop.goal: A ranked, evidence-backed shortlist for one open role.
loop.verify: Every candidate scored against the same published rubric, with a second reviewer agent re-scoring independently; any unscored candidate blocks the shortlist.
loop.stop: The shortlist clears the bar, or the pool runs dry — then it reports what the market actually has rather than padding the list.
